verbalization: Ibuprofen appears to have a dual relationship with A2780cisR, as it is linked through two distinct pathways. In the first pathway, Ibuprofen targets Carnitine O-palmitoyltransferase 1, muscle isoform, which in turn is targeted by a protein with the identifier CDAISMWEOUEBRE-LKPKBOIGSA-N. This protein ultimately targets A2780cisR. In the second pathway, Ibuprofen directly targets Ribosomal protein S6 kinase 2, which is targeted by 2-Cyclohexen-1-one, 3,5,5-trimethyl-4-methylene-, a compound that also targets A2780cisR. Both pathways suggest that Ibuprofen may influence A2780cisR through different molecular mechanisms, potentially involving cellular processes such as protein synthesis or metabolic regulation. The integration of these pathways highlights the complexity of Ibuprofen's interaction with A2780cisR, emphasizing the importance of considering multiple layers of molecular interaction in drug-target analysis.
